nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r$ be points of Euclidean 3-space and let $T$ be a triangle in Euclidean 3-space whose vertices, in order, are $p$, $q$ and $r$. Then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ equals the circumradius of $T$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius of a triangle

nodes.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space and the set $\{p, q, r\}$ is collinear, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Collinear points have infinite extended circumradius

nodes.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space with $p = q$, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Equal first two points give infinite extended circumradius

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(r, q, p)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is invariant under reversal

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(q, p, r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the first two points

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, r, q)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the last two points

nodes.summary: For every vector $v$ and all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(v + p, v + q, v + r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Translation invariance of the extended circumradius

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is the following value in $[0, \infty]$. If $p, q, r$ are affinely independent, it is the circumradius of the triangle with vertices $p$, $q$ and $r$. Otherwise, that is, when the three points are collinear (in particular when two of them coincide), it is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius of three points

nodes.summary: Let $a \le b$ be real numbers and let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space that is continuously differentiable on $[a, b]$. Then the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ equals $\int_a^b \lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert \, dt$.
nodes.title: Contour length of a $C^1$ curve

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space and let $a, b$ be real numbers. The contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the total variation of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$: the supremum, over all finite sequences $t_0 \le t_1 \le \dots \le t_n$ of points of $[a, b]$, of $\sum_{i < n} \lVert \gamma(t_{i+1}) - \gamma(t_i) \rVert$. It is a value in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Contour length

nodes.summary: If an oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram, then its crossing number is finite: the alternating representative is itself a regular projection.
nodes.title: Alternating link types have finite crossing number

nodes.summary: If an oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram, then its crossing number equals some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Alternating link types have a natural-number crossing number

nodes.summary: The constant $c = 0$ is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality.
nodes.title: Zero is an admissible alternating constant

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n$ and every oriented labeled link type with $n$ components that admits an alternating diagram and whose crossing number is a natural number $k$, the ropelength of the type is at least $c k$.
nodes.title: Admissible constants for the tight alternating knot inequality

nodes.summary: The real number $0$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality between the ropelength and the crossing number of link types.
nodes.title: Zero is an admissible tight-knot constant

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the crossing number of $L$ equals $k$, the ropelength of $L$ is at least $c \, k^{3/4}$, the inequality being read in $[0, \infty]$. Here the crossing number and the ropelength of $L$ are those of its oriented labeled…
nodes.title: Admissible constants for the tight-knot inequality

nodes.summary: Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot constant. Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality is at most the tight alternating knot constant.
nodes.title: Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: Let $C_{22a}$ be the tight knot constant. Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies $c \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: Admissible constants are bounded by the tight knot constant

nodes.summary: If a real number $c$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with $0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality as well.
nodes.title: Admissibility passes to smaller nonnegative constants

nodes.summary: Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among nonnegative reals. If a real number $c$ is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with $0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is admissible as well.
nodes.title: Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm.
nodes.title: Euclidean 3-space

nodes.summary: For a curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a, b$, the ropelength ratio of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ divided by the thickness of the trace $\gamma([a, b])$. The quotient is taken in $[0, \infty]$, where $c / 0 = \infty$ for $c \ne 0$, $0 / 0 = 0$ and $c / \infty = 0$.
nodes.title: Ropelength ratio

nodes.summary: If $s \subseteq t$ are sets in Euclidean 3-space, then the thickness of $t$ is at most the thickness of $s$: enlarging a set can only add triples and hence can only decrease the infimum.
nodes.title: Thickness is antitone

nodes.summary: The empty subset of Euclidean 3-space has thickness $\infty$, as an empty infimum in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Thickness of the empty set

nodes.summary: For every set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space and all points $p, q, r \in s$, the thickness of $s$ is at most the extended circumradius of $p, q, r$.
nodes.title: Thickness is at most every circumradius

nodes.summary: For every point $p$ of Euclidean 3-space, the set $\{p\}$ has thickness $\infty$: its only triple $(p, p, p)$ is degenerate.
nodes.title: Thickness of a single point

nodes.summary: The thickness of a set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the extended circumradii of $(p, q, r)$ over all points $p, q, r \in s$. Since the extended circumradius of three collinear points (in particular of three points two of which coincide) is $\infty$, this is also the infimum over the triples of pairwise distinct points of $s$.
nodes.title: Thickness

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the tight alternating knot constant is at most $b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: The tight alternating knot constant $C_{22b} = b_0$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the set of real numbers $c$ admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality: those $c \ge 0$ such that every link type $K$ that admits an alternating diagram and has finite crossing number $\mathrm{Cr}(K)$ has ropelength $\mathrm{L}(K) \ge c\,\mathrm{Cr}(K)$. The supremum is not assumed to be attained.
nodes.title: Tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies $C_{22a} \le b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the tight knot constant

nodes.summary: The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ that are admissible for the tight-knot inequality $\mathrm{ropelength} \ge c \cdot (\text{crossing number})^{3/4}$ on link types. The supremum is not assumed to be attained.
nodes.title: Tight knot constant

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space whose ordered triple $(p, q, r)$ is affinely independent, the triangle in Euclidean 3-space with vertices $p$, $q$, $r$, in that order.
nodes.title: Triangle on three affinely independent points

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the family indexed by $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that sends $0 \mapsto p$, $1 \mapsto q$ and $2 \mapsto r$.
nodes.title: Ordered triple of points

nodes.summary: The tight alternating knot constant, an extended real number, is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The tight alternating knot constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies $0 \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: The tight knot constant is nonnegative
